title: Why a Fresh Pre-Buy Protects a Buyer's Position
hook: A pre-buy inspection isn't a formality. It's leverage.
body:
Most negotiating power in an aircraft transaction shifts the moment the pre-buy findings come back. A thorough, independent inspection gives a buyer an accurate picture of the aircraft's true condition — not the seller's version of it, not the logbook summary, the actual state of the airframe, engines, and systems.

That picture is what lets you negotiate from fact instead of assumption. Discrepancies found during a pre-buy aren't obstacles — they're information. They tell you what to fix, what to price in, and what to walk away from.

Skipping or shortcutting this step to move faster almost always costs more later, in unplanned maintenance, in resale value, or in disputes that could have been settled before closing.

Know the aircraft's condition before you're asked to defend your offer — or your exit.
